questions.q: What daily habit did Franklin create to keep learning part of every weekday?
a: An hour each weekday spent reading, writing and reflecting
Two hours each morning memorizing passages
A weekly debate with other printers
Daily letters to a mentor in London
questions.why: The summary calls this his five-hour rule: one hour on each of five activities per week.

questions.q: Why did Franklin stay at his printing job with Samuel Keimer?
a: Their long philosophical talks sharpened his debating and speaking
The position paid far better than other shops
His family expected him to remain there
It gave him control of a Boston newspaper
questions.why: He had joined to improve his writing but stayed for the conversations.

questions.q: How did seventeen-year-old Franklin get his early essays published?
a: He invented a female alter ego named Silence Dogood
He signed them with his brother's name
He paid the newspaper to print them anonymously
He submitted them as letters from a Boston merchant
questions.why: The summary says no one would have taken a teenage boy seriously, so he created a persona.

questions.q: What lesson does the summary draw about learning from Franklin's example?
a: If you truly want to learn, you will find a way
Formal schooling is the only reliable path
You should wait for a publisher before writing
Natural talent matters more than daily effort
questions.why: The summary insists that lack of a publisher, agent or school is no longer a valid excuse.

questions.q: What did Franklin petition for in 1790, the year he died?
a: That American liberty be upheld without distinction of color
That the colonies adopt his model of government
That a national university be founded
That printing apprenticeships be shortened
questions.why: The summary notes he wanted slavery abolished, which happened seventy-five years later.
